stages.label: inv1
stages.notes:
Change made: fixed the bug in `context/harness/scripts/summarize.py`, the "house method" script that `AGENTS.md` instructs the agent to run and blindly trust ("Do not compute the total yourself. The script is the house method.").

Moment that motivated it: in `context/rollouts/base1.md`, the agent follows AGENTS.md exactly — reads `ledger.csv` (rows `100.25,posted`, `-20.10,posted`, `5.00,posted`), runs `python3 scripts/summarize.py ledger.csv`, gets `Total: 105.25`, and writes that straight to `answer.txt` without question (`context/deliverables/base1/answer.txt` = "Total: 105.25"). The correct signed sum per `context/task.md` ("Sum the signed amounts. A value in parentheses is negative. Skip rows whose status is void.") is 100.25 − 20.10 + 5.00 = 85.15. The old script computed `sum(amount for amount in rows if amount > 0)` — it silently dropped every negative entry instead of summing it with its sign, and never implemented parentheses-as-negative or void-skipping at all. The one available rollout shows the agent complying with AGENTS.md's "don't compute it yourself, trust the script" instruction to the letter and landing on a wrong answer as a direct, deterministic consequence — not an agent mistake, a broken tool mistake.

Why this is the right lever for the INV dimension: the mission explicitly assigns `scripts/<name>.py` to this dimension as the home for "repeated deterministic extraction, conversion or checking, with clear inputs, outputs and failure behavior." The script's whole job (its stated contract, per both task.md and the AGENTS.md framing of it as "the house method") was to compute exactly this signed/parens/void sum — it just didn't actually do that. Fixing it doesn't add a new domain rule or professional judgment call; it makes an existing owned component meet the one specification already given, so the existing AGENTS.md instruction to delegate arithmetic to the script (good practice — keeps the LLM from hand-computing sums on potentially larger ledgers) becomes safe to keep as-is.

Also relevant: per the "ground it in this workspace" guidance, this harness is filed in the domain library and will be read as an example for other ledger-reconciliation tasks, which may actually contain parentheses or void rows (this particular `ledger.csv` sample happens to have neither). A script that only coincidentally produced a plausible-looking number on this one ledger, but implemented none of the stated parens/void rules, would silently misreconcile the next ledger that uses either convention. The fix implements both rules directly (strip `()`→negate; skip rows where `status` lowercased is `void`), scoped tightly to what task.md actually specifies — no invented extras like currency symbols or thousands separators, since nothing in the evidence calls for them.

No other component changed. AGENTS.md's three-step procedure, the scripts/README.md, .codex/README.md, and sub_agents/README.md placeholders were all consistent with a correct script and didn't need edits — with only one rollout available and no sign of skipped prose, there's no evidence basis for a hook, skill, or subagent, and adding always-on text here would just be prose for a problem the script fix already removes. Verified the corrected script against `context/source/ledger.csv` directly: now prints `Total: 85.15`.

stages.label: dom1
stages.notes:
Change made: fixed `context/harness/scripts/summarize.py`, the deterministic "house method" helper that `AGENTS.md` instructs the agent to trust blindly ("Do not compute the total yourself. The script is the house method.").

Moment that motivated it: in `context/rollouts/base1.md`, the agent followed AGENTS.md exactly — ran `scripts/summarize.py ledger.csv`, got `Total: 105.25`, and wrote it verbatim to `answer.txt` (confirmed in `context/deliverables/base1/answer.txt`). This is wrong per the task's own definition of reconciliation ("Sum the signed amounts. A value in parentheses is negative. Skip rows whose status is void."):

- The old script was `sum(Decimal(r["amount"]) for r in rows if Decimal(r["amount"]) > 0)` — it only summed *positive* amounts, discarding negative ones entirely instead of summing the signed total. On the real `context/source/ledger.csv` (100.25 posted, -20.10 posted, 5.00 posted), the correct signed sum is 85.15, but the script returned 105.25 (dropping the -20.10 row completely). This is a deterministic, repeated failure: every rollout that obeys AGENTS.md's "do not compute it yourself" instruction and trusts this script will reproduce the same wrong number.
- The old script also had no status filter at all, so a `void` row would have been included rather than skipped, contradicting the task's explicit rule.
- I verified separately that Python's `Decimal` constructor does *not* accept accounting-style parentheses (`Decimal('(123.45)')` raises `decimal.ConversionSyntax`), so the old script would have crashed outright on any ledger using parenthesized negatives — which the task explicitly says is a valid input form, even though this particular instance's `ledger.csv` happens not to use that notation.

Fix: rewrote the script to (1) strip a `(...)` wrapper and negate the value when present, (2) sum every row's signed amount, and (3) skip rows whose `status` (trimmed, case-insensitive) is `void`. Verified: on the real workspace `ledger.csv` it now prints `Total: 85.15` (was `105.25`); on a synthetic ledger with both a `void` parenthetical row and a non-void parenthetical row, it correctly excludes the void row and negates the other, producing `84.15`.

I treated this as a domain-correctness fix (the script encodes the authoritative reconciliation formula from `task.md`, not a procedural/invocation concern), per the ENCODING guidance that names "a SCRIPT for a deterministic operation the runs hand-rolled and got wrong" as the preferred fix form — this is exactly that case, caught directly in the one available trajectory.

No change to `AGENTS.md`: once the script matches the task's own definition, the existing instruction to trust the script and transcribe its output verbatim is the right practitioner behavior (it prevents manual-arithmetic slips) and needed no edit. No evidence in the single rollout motivated adding a skill, subagent, or hook — this is a single small deterministic computation with no recognizable recurring-trigger shape beyond the one script, so KEEP_BASE on every other component.

adopted -> fix scripts/summarize.py (identical in both inv1 and dom1 candidates) -> context/rollouts/base1.md: agent follows AGENTS.md's "Do not compute the total yourself. The script is the house method." instruction exactly, runs the old script, gets `Total: 105.25`, and writes it verbatim to answer.txt (confirmed in context/deliverables/base1/answer.txt). The old script was `sum(amount for amount in rows if amount > 0)` — it discarded every negative row instead of summing it with sign, and had no void-skip or parentheses-negative handling at all, despite task.md explicitly requiring both ("A value in parentheses is negative. Skip rows whose status is void."). This is a deterministic defect in an owned script, not model variance: every run that obeys the trust-the-script instruction reproduces the same wrong number, and separately verified `Decimal("(20.10)")` raises `ConversionSyntax`, so the old script would crash outright on any ledger using the parenthetical-negative convention the task names as valid.
kept -> AGENTS.md's "run the script, don't hand-compute, write it verbatim" procedure -> once the script's behavior matches task.md's own definition, this instruction is correct and keeps the agent from introducing manual-arithmetic slips; both pool/inv1/decisions.md and pool/dom1/decisions.md independently reached the same conclusion and left AGENTS.md untouched, and both candidate rollouts (pool/inv1/rollout.md, pool/dom1/rollout.md) show the agent following it and landing on the correct `Total: 85.15`, confirmed against context/source/ledger.csv (100.25 − 20.10 + 5.00 = 85.15).
kept -> no skill/subagent/hook added -> single small deterministic computation with one script and one trigger path; neither candidate's single rollout nor the base rollout shows any recurring, skippable, or in-loop-enforcement problem that would justify the cost of an always-on or on-demand component beyond the script fix itself.

seq.why: trivial pool: single final at k=1; delivered without a selector session

experience.cue: a harness instructs the agent to trust and transcribe the output of an owned deterministic script ("don't compute it yourself, the script is the house method"), and the task spec states a formula (signed sum, parenthetical negatives, status-based exclusion) that the script is supposed to implement.
experience.lesson: before trusting an instruction that tells the agent to defer to a script, read the script itself against the task's own stated formula line-by-line (every clause: sign handling, notation variants, filter conditions) — a script that passes on the one sample input can still silently drop or mis-handle cases (negative rows, parenthetical notation, excluded statuses) that the sample doesn't exercise, and the fix belongs in the script, not in the instruction telling the agent to trust it.
experience.evidence: scripts/summarize.py row above — base_harness's script implemented only the "sum positive amounts" fragment of the task formula and dropped negatives entirely with no void-skip or parens handling; base1's rollout (trusting the unfixed script) produced a wrong, deterministic `105.25` on every run, while the fixed script (identical across all three pool candidates) produced the correct `85.15`.
experience.confidence: high — the contrast is a direct before/after on the same script and same ledger input (base1 vs. the three pool rollouts), isolating the one component that changed, with no other file differing between the wrong-answer and right-answer runs.
